To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

corporate social responsibility is more likely to occur when the following conditions are met: (1) when there is an active public and private regulatory system in place, (2) when there is a strong civil society, (3) when there are institutionalized norms regarding socially responsible behavior, and (4) when there are associative behaviors among corporations themselves.
corporate social responsibility is positively related to the presence of public and private regulation and to the presence of nONGovernmental and other organizations that monitor corporate activity.
the relationship between economic conditions and corporate social responsibility is mediated by institutional conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the institutional conditions under which corporations will behave in ways that are socially responsible.
the question of why corporations would behave in socially responsible or socially irresponsible ways.
how the behavior of firms and the structure of the market economy are shaped by the social and political institutions in which firms operate and by the behavior of firms themselves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

corporate social responsibility is likely to be a function of the following institutional conditions: the presence of public regulation, private regulation, monitoring by nongovernmental organizations, associative behavior among firms, and organized stakeholder dialogues.
corporate social responsibility is most likely when there are strong institutional constraints on corporate behavior.

the likelihood of corporate behavior in socially responsible ways depends upon the extent to which basic economic conditions, public and private regulation (including the existence of a regulatory state), the presence of nongoovernmental organizations that monitor corporate activity, institutionalized norms of behavior, associative behavior, and organized dialog among corporations and their various stakeholders are all present and functioning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
corporate social responsibility is a complex phenomenon that depends upon a complex interaction of economic and institutional factors.
corporate social responsibility is a function of the interaction between the institutional and economic environments.
the institutional theory of corporate behavior is an alternative to the economic theory of corporate behavior, and that the two theories are complementary, not mutually exclusive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
corporate social responsibility is not a matter of corporate goodwill or altruism. Rather, it is a response to the social and institutional conditions in which the corporation is embedded.

corporations are more likely to behave in a socially responsible way when they face a combination of strong public regulation and private monitoring and when they face weak institutionalized norms regarding corporate behavior.
the institutional conditions under which socially responsible behavior is likely to occur are not necessarily those that would be predicted by a purely economic model.
